raw_response:
I’m 48 this year, and I’ve only farmed on my own for 4 years, so I still lean a lot on what works locally. On 200 mu, I won’t spread myself too fancy. I’ll keep the main area in wheat-maize because that’s the most stable cash flow here, and I know how to manage it with machinery and the well. I’ll leave smaller blocks for cabbage and stevia, because they can make more money, but they also need more hands and the price can move around. If I put too much land into those cash crops and the market turns bad or labor gets tight, that’s trouble.

So this year I’d do about 130 mu in wheat-maize rotation, 35 mu cabbage, and 35 mu stevia. For wheat and maize, I’ll stay close to the local pattern: fertilizer not too low, because underfeeding is more dangerous than spending a bit extra, but I also won’t chase very high rates. Irrigation from the well is useful, but pumping costs money, so I’ll water at key stages instead of flooding whenever I feel uneasy. Cabbage gets more fertilizer and more labor because if I want a good head, I can’t be stingy. Stevia I’ll keep moderate, because it’s a cash crop but I don’t want to over-invest before I see how the stand looks and what the buying price is.
